from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism of Coordinate Transformation", 
                          ["We map old to new coordinates.", 
                           "The change-of-basis matrix is P.", 
                           "P columns are new basis vectors.", 
                           "Robot dogs use P to navigate.", 
                           "Matrix P translates local steps globally."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # v_new = P v_old
        equation = MathTex(r"v_{new} = P v_{old}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # P in yellow
        matrix_p = MathTex(r"P", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p, 'C3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Indicate(matrix_p))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # P columns are new basis vectors
        matrix_p_cols = MathTex(r"P = \begin{bmatrix} \vec{i}' & \vec{j}' \end{bmatrix}", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p_cols, 'B4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(matrix_p, matrix_p_cols))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Robot Navigator + Asset
        robot = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg")

        self.place_at_grid(group, 'D5', scale_factor=0.6)

        self.lecture[3].set_color("#87CEFA")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Robot navigating with matrix P
        vec = Vector(UP * 1 + RIGHT * 1, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(vec, 'C5', scale_factor=0.9)
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#4682B4", "stroke_opacity": 0.5})

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Formula: v_B equals P inverse v_A.", "P transforms new to old.", "Inverse converts old to new.", "A camera lens frame is new.", "Pixels map to world view."]
        self.setup_layout("The Change-of-Basis Formula", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        formula = MathTex(r"[v]_B", "=", "P^{-1}", r"[v]_A", font_size=36)
        
        # Assets
        lens = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lens.svg")
        pixels = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pixels.svg")
        camera = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/camera.svg")
        
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid['C4'], end=self.grid['C5'], color=WHITE)
        eq_sign = formula[1]
        
        # Grid visual group (for criticism fix #24)
        grid_group = VGroup(formula, lens, pixels, camera, arrow)
        self.place_in_area(grid_group, 'A2', 'F6', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Formula placement (fix #25)
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'A4', 'C6', scale_factor=0.75)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFA500")
        formula[2].set_color("#FFA500") # P
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#87CEFA")
        formula[2].set_color("#87CEFA") # Inverse P
        self.play(Indicate(formula[2])) 
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(lens, 'D2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.add(lens)
        self.play(FadeIn(lens))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#32CD32")
        self.place_at_grid(pixels, 'D4', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(camera, 'D6', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8) # Fix #23
        self.play(FadeIn(pixels), FadeIn(camera), GrowArrow(arrow))
        
        self.play(eq_sign.animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Conceptual Application", ["The vector itself never changes.", "Only its coordinate description shifts.", "Key for graphics and PCA."])
        
        # Load asset
        grid_asset = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg")
        
        # Setup visual elements
        axes_a = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        axes_b = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        vector = Arrow(ORIGIN, [1, 1, 0], color=YELLOW)
        
        group_a = VGroup(axes_a, vector.copy(), grid_asset.copy())
        group_b = VGroup(axes_b, vector.copy(), grid_asset.copy())
        
        # Initial positions
        self.place_in_area(group_a, 'C4', 'D5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_in_area(group_b, 'E4', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#D3D3D3"))
        self.play(Create(group_a), Create(group_b))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#D3D3D3"))
        self.play(group_b.animate.rotate(PI/4))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#D3D3D3"))
        # Scale grid of group_b relative to group_a
        self.play(group_b[2].animate.scale(1.2))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (1 Minute)
sections.content: Briefly define a basis as a 'coordinate system'. Use a 2D grid overlay to show that any vector can be reached using basis vectors (i, j). Introduce the core question: 'How do we describe the same physical vector if we change our perspective (basis)?'
sections.example: Visualize a treasure map where the 'grid' lines are rotated. Even if the grid changes, the 'X marks the spot' location in the world remains the same.

sections.title: The Mechanism of Coordinate Transformation (1.5 Minutes)
sections.content: Explain that a coordinate transformation is essentially mapping 'Old Coordinates' to 'New Coordinates' using a Change-of-Basis Matrix (P). Visualize P as columns of new basis vectors expressed in terms of the old basis.
sections.example: Imagine a robot dog moving in a square room. If the dog's local 'forward' direction changes, we use matrix P to translate its 'local' steps into the 'global' room coordinates.

sections.title: The Change-of-Basis Formula (1.5 Minutes)
sections.content: Formulate the equation: [v]_B = P_inv * [v]_A. Use animation to show the multiplication of the matrix against the vector. Emphasize that P represents the transformation from New to Old, so its inverse is required to convert Old to New.
sections.example: Use a camera analogy: The object is the vector. The 'Old Basis' is the world frame, and the 'New Basis' is the camera's lens frame. P allows the computer to calculate where pixels appear in the camera view.

sections.title: Summary & Conceptual Application (1 Minute)
sections.content: Conclude by emphasizing that the vector v is invariant—it doesn't change; only its description changes. Reiterate that this is the mathematical foundation for computer graphics (rotating objects) and data analysis (PCA).
sections.example: Final visual: A 3D character rotating in a game engine. Show how 'Change of Basis' is what allows the game to calculate the character's limbs relative to their own body, rather than the static game world.
